analysis:
The PR adds one env var, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED, to the LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list (LaunchAgent.swift head lines ~276-279 comment, line 295 entry). It also documents the var in docs/reference/configuration.md line 414. The var only selects a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel for Qwen3.5-family models: stock kernel, forced packed or rows kernel, or a parity probe. It carries no secrets, credentials, paths or URLs. It is read once per process by the SDK reader (GatedDeltaPrefill.mode), which is not in the supplied evidence.

Security considerations: the allow-list forwards a value from the invoking shell into the launchd plist. This follows the existing pattern of other passthrough keys such as MIMO and prefix-cache flags. The operator is already the adversary for local settings (ADV-001, TB-003), and the var cannot expand attestation, authorization or encryption scope. Per the docs, forced kernels skip the bit-exactness parity check and are labelled A/B measurement only. An operator could therefore force a non-parity kernel and alter numerical output. That is already within T-007 (a malicious provider serving manipulated outputs) and the T-056 overclaim limits. It is not a new capability, since an operator can already modify the process environment or run arbitrary code. It does not touch the prefix-cache storage, TTL, HMAC naming or encryption paths in T-041, and it does not interact with cache KEK handling or A-016 authorization.

Open integration questions: (1) The kernel-selection code in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift is outside the supplied units, so the claim that the default probe preserves bit-exact outputs is unverified. (2) The tail of the changed patch excerpt for the docs file was truncated, but the visible head lines cover the change. No regression was identified.
